reading.body:
Flexential Dallas - Downtown Dallas publishes 6.66 MW of IT capacity across 80,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 6.66 MW supports roughly 166 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, the same power supports roughly 666 racks. Those figures are assumptions about rack density, not operator claims. The campus is a mid-sized facility, not a hyperscale build, and the published power ceiling limits how many GPU-dense nodes it can absorb before power, not floor space, becomes the binding constraint.

The certifications tell a specific story about qualified workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SSAE 18 qualify the campus for financial-controls audits. SOC 2 Type 2 qualifies it for security, availability, and confidentiality attestations. HITRUST qualifies it for regulated healthcare data. Together these certifications point toward enterprise and compliance-sensitive tenants rather than toward the unregulated, high-density AI training clusters that typically seek raw megawatts over audit frameworks.

Within Texas, this campus ranks 13th out of 15 facilities for which this site has read a published megawatt figure, contributing 6.66 MW against a state total of 399.41 MW across those 15 facilities, a share of roughly 1.7 percent. Texas has 133 facilities mapped in OpenStreetMap but only 15 have published a capacity figure, so the state total is a floor, not a ceiling. At its current published size, this campus is not a meaningful mover of Texas AI compute capacity, but its certifications position it for the regulated-workload segment of the market where raw scale is not the primary selection criterion.
